    Former Hawk signs with AFL-aligned SANFL side following VFL premiership

    Henry Hustwaite will trade the brown and gold of Box Hill for the Crows’ tricolours.

    By
    Harrison McIlwaine
    -
    WRITER | November 27, 2026 - 1:16pm
    2,745
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:51
    Instaread

    Former Hawk Henry Hustwaite has accepted a post with the SANFL Crows, joining the West Lakes outfit's reserves affiliate as its marquee signing.

    The 22-year-old midfielder is no stranger to excellence at the reserves level, having claimed best and fairest honours for the Box Hill Hawks this season, in what was a premiership-winning campaign.

    Unfortunately, "The Pencil" could never quite translate dominance at that level to the elite competition, yielding 11 appearances for Sam Mitchell's senior side since his 2022 drafting.

    Now, the Dandenong Stingrays product will ply his trade for Michael Godden's outfit.

    “Henry is a classy player who can play through the midfield or across half-back, and his clean hands and decision-making really stand out,” Crows GM Football Operations and Compliance Tom Hurley said.

    “His form at VFL level over the past two seasons speaks for itself, and he's shown he can consistently win the ball and influence games.”

    “Importantly, Henry has spent four years in an AFL environment and understands the standards required.

    "That experience will be valuable for our developing players, and we're excited to have someone of his quality headline our SANFL squad in 2027.”

    Should Hustwaite impress in his new environment, there are avenues for elevation to the Crows' senior list, with the 2027 Mid-Season Draft one such option.

    He may also be considered for an SSP train-on audition, potentially joining the likes of former St Kilda backman James Van Es, who looms as cover for the recently departed Jordon Butts, as uncertainty continues to surround Nick Murray.

    As prolific as they come, Hustwaite's lowest disposal tally in the recent VFL season was 22, and Round 19 of the 2025 season was the last time he registered fewer than 20 touches.

    Adelaide has also committed to signing Hawks father-son prospect Kobe Williams as a First Nations Category B Rookie.
